interest: Shows how Cold War diplomacy and Soviet objections halted Allied occupation marine wildlife research off Japan.
keywords: SCAP (Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers)
overview: This file documents the planning, diplomatic negotiations, and ultimate cancellation of a SCAP Natural Resources Section scientific fur seal expedition off the coast of Japan between November 1948 and June 1949. Originally intended to take up to 1,000 seals to examine feeding habits and migration patterns, the research plan was reduced to 200 animals following United States coordination with Canada and notification to the Soviet Union. In response to formal Soviet diplomatic objections opposing any killing of seals prior to concluding a new multilateral convention, the United States instructed SCAP to terminate the operation after taking only 21 or 22 specimens. The remaining documents trace subsequent intergovernmental communications, discussions regarding a draft international fur seal convention, and the transfer of the collected pelts and skulls to the Department of the Interior and the U.S. National Museum for scientific comparison with Pribilof herds.
